paragraph: The African Union's [register](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, records Angola as having ratified it on 21 February 2020 and deposited the instrument on 11 May 2020. Angola's [Resolution 33/19 of 9 July 2019](<https://angolex.com/paginas/resolucoes/convencao-da-uniao-africana-sobre-ciberseguranca-e-proteccao-de-dados-33a-19a.html>) is the national instrument on the convention. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national law, decree or regulation passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Operating would need such a law, decree or regulation passed or amended.

The African Union's [register](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, shows no signature, ratification or deposit for Burundi. The convention has been in force since 8 June 2023. Participants at a [workshop in Bujumbura in February 2026](<https://communityvoice.bi/1489-2/>) called on the government to ratify it. No change in Burundi's position has been found in the last twelve months. No national law passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Preparing would need a signed African legal text on a digital matter, or a named regional act that binds Burundi.

It records ratification on 14 May 2024 and deposit on 12 November 2024. A [paper to a National Assembly workshop in January 2024](<https://julienhounkpe.info/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Contribution0.pdf>) said Benin's digital code omits parts of a 2010 ECOWAS act on personal data protection. The paper named its rules on sensitive data and on transfers abroad. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national law passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Operating would need such a law, decree or regulation passed or amended.

The Central African monetary union validated a shared [QR-code payment standard](<https://leconomie.info/article/paiement-numerique-le-gimac-officialise-la-norme-qr-code-interoperable-de-la-cemac>) in April 2026, and launched it on 29 July 2026 for six member states. The Central African Republic is named among them. An [ACTPOL brief of September 2026](<https://www.actpol.org/research/central-africa-laws-before-regulators-cameroon>), citing the African Union's register of 2 February 2026, says the country has taken no action on the Malabo Convention. It has neither signed nor ratified it. In the last twelve months the standard was validated and launched, and the brief reported no signature. No national law giving effect to a shared African text has been found. Establishing would need the country to ratify or accede to such a text, by a law or decree approving it or by depositing the instrument.
